title: Integrity Forensics Report
description: The synthesized output of a /anti-autoresearch run. Produced by tools/adjudicate_findings.py (deterministic) from the union of all skills' findings. The overall_verdict is computed by RULES, not by an LLM — this is the structural defense against 'LLM slop grading LLM slop'.

taxonomy_version.description: Version of references/hack-pattern-taxonomy.md used — recorded so a report is interpretable after the taxonomy evolves.

overall_verdict.description: Deliberately NOT 'fabricated/honest'. CLEAN_GIVEN_EVIDENCE = no flags at the available observability level (NOT 'the paper is honest'). SOFT_FLAGS = minor/medium-FP-risk discrepancies a reviewer should ask about. HARD_FLAGS = ≥1 span-anchored critical discrepancy decidable at this observability level.

adjudicator.description: e.g. "deterministic-rules-v0" — the rule engine + version, never an LLM identity.

adversarial_memo.description: Evidence-bound rejection memo from adversarial-case-builder. Informational; contributes NO verdict weight.

downgraded_for_observability.description: How many findings the adjudicator demoted because the run's evidence tier was below the finding's required level.

limitations.description: What this run could NOT check (always populated — honesty is part of the contract).

human_review_required.description: Always true. The report is decision SUPPORT for a human reviewer/AC; it never issues a verdict on misconduct.

coverage.description: Per-skill run status from the orchestrating workflow: completed | not_applicable | review_unavailable. A verdict-bearing dimension marked review_unavailable blocks the acquittal (overall_verdict REVIEW_UNAVAILABLE instead of CLEAN_GIVEN_EVIDENCE); found flags still stand. Keys are whitelisted — an unknown key is rejected by the adjudicator (a typo must not bypass the gate).

coverage_provenance.description: Binds every `coverage` entry marked completed to the claims.json (evidence ledger) state PRESENT AT ADJUDICATION TIME — sha256 over paper_id/observability_level/ledger_version/source_files/claim content, via tools/adjudicate_findings.py --coverage + --ledger (issue #17 #1; independent of --manifest). SCOPE NOTE: this is the ledger this run was adjudicated against, not literally the exact state a given auditor read at its own completion time (no auditor stamps a per-run ledger snapshot into coverage.json). NOT A GUARANTEE: the workflow documents a RULE that a stale-ledger rebuild deletes coverage.json, but that rule is instruction-level, not mechanically enforced (the Step-2 init code uses setdefault, which only fills missing keys and would not wipe a stale completed entry if the delete step were skipped) — this hash proves only that the coverage map is internally consistent with the ledger it was adjudicated against, not that the ledger is fresh. Keys are a SUBSET of `coverage`'s: not_applicable and review_unavailable entries never appear here — a hash on either would falsely imply the ledger was read. HONEST LIMITATION: every auditor consumes the full ledger today (no per-dimension claim subsetting exists), so every completed skill key maps to the SAME whole-ledger hash; the per-skill shape is forward-compatible with real per-dimension scoping, not evidence that it exists. Empty object when coverage is absent/empty or the ledger has no source_files/claims to bind to. Keys are whitelisted, matching `coverage`.

audited_content_fingerprint.description: sha256 over the present pdf/latex/bib artifacts (via tools/adjudicate_findings.py --manifest, sourced from artifact_manifest.json's already-computed hashes, strictly validated including a paper_id match and a real-boolean present check), so a downstream gate can verify this report was generated from THIS paper content rather than replayed onto edited text (issue #17 #2). SCOPE NOTE: bounded by artifact_manifest.json's own scan depth (root + one subdirectory level, build_manifest.py's pre-existing documented limitation) — a paper whose LaTeX is split deeper is not fully covered by this field alone (coverage_provenance's claim-content hashing partially compensates in practice). null when --manifest was omitted or named zero present content artifacts.

critical_refutation_coverage.description: Counters for the critical-refutation pass over LLM-proposed weight-1 criticals: eligible/completed/unavailable/malformed/contested. eligible>completed adds a limitation; CONTESTED never changes severity or the verdict.

critical_countercheck.description: Counters for the deterministic counter-check over allow-listed LLM criticals. proved_compatible = demoted to info by a computation (the ONLY path that may demote a critical); basis_invalid = accusation demoted to major for an unauditable numeric basis.
